PUBLIC COMMENT
Citizens wishing to address the City Council and Successor Agency on any item on the agenda or on any matter
not on the agenda may do so at this time. State law (Government Code Section 54950 et seq.) prohibits the City
Council from taking action or engaging in discussion on a specific item unless it appears on a posted agenda .
Upon request, the City Council may, in their discretion, allow citizen participation on a specific item on the agenda
at the time the item is considered by the City Council. If you wish to address the City Council /Successor Agency
at this time, please complete a speaker's card and give it to the City Clerk prior to commencement of the City
Council meeting. Please limit your remarks to three (3) minutes.

To increase the effectiveness of the Public Comment Period, the following rules shall be followed: No person shall
make any remarks which result in disrupting, disturbing or otherwise impeding the meeting.

  CONSENT CALENDAR
Items under the Consent Calendar are considered to be routine and may be enacted by one motion. There will be
no discussion of these items unless members of the Public or City Council request specific items to be removed
from the Consent Agenda for a separate discussion. lf the item is desired to be discussed separately, it should be
the first item under Scheduled Matters.

AGENDA ITEMS AND ACTIONS
PUBLIC COMMENT ON CLOSED SESSION ITEMS There were no individuals wishing to address the City Council on any items on the Closed Session agenda. 

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION The City Council recessed to Closed Session at 6:44 p.m.

RECONVENE TO OPEN SESSION City Council reconvened to Open session at 9:26 p.m.

ORAL CLOSED SESSION ANNOUNCEMENT City Attorney Tapia reported on Closed Session items: 

Items #1, #2 and #4 - staff provided a presentation, the direction was provided, and no reportable action was taken on any of these items. 

Item #2.C was not discussed.  

Item s#2.A and 2.B - staff provided a presentation, the direction was provided, and no reportable action was taken.

6:00 P.M. - CITY COUNCIL MEETING

CALL TO ORDER Mayor Rebollo called meeting to order at 6:01 p.m.

ROLL CALL Councilmember Altamirano and Vice Mayor Argumedo attended the meeting via teleconferencing.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE Claude McFerguson led the Pledge of Allegiance.

INVOCATION Mayor Rebollo offered the invocation.

APPEARANCES AND PRESENTATIONS

10.. Presentation/Update from the Sheriff's Department Regarding Public Safety in the City of Commerce Sergeant Duarte provided an overview of the statistics for the last month. There were five robberies, seven burglaries, and 18 grand theft. There were 26 felony arrests and 21 misdemeanor arrests. There was an increase in crime from January of last year. 

Mayor Rebollo asked for a status update on Special Problems Unit activities for January. Councilmember Lainez wondered whether the increase in crime in Commerce is similar to neighboring jurisdictions, and Sergeant Duarte stated that it increased in the other cities as well. Further discussion took place, and requests were made to see statistics regarding arrests related to crime areas - how many crimes occurred and how many were resolved. 


1.. Commendation Honoring Breanna Lizarraga for her Countless Achievements and Being Named the Libero of the Year in the South Coast Conference. Mayor and Council recognized Breanna Lizarraga for her achievements.

PUBLIC COMMENT There were no individuals wishing to address the City Council on any items within their jurisdiction. 




CONSENT CALENDAR  -  Action: adopt (Pass) Moved by Kevin Lainez Councilmember Altamirano pulled item #5 from the Consent Calendar, Councilmember Lainez pulled item #6 and Mayor Rebollo pulled item #8.

Item #5 - Councilmember Altamirano recused himself from participating on this item due to the potential conflict.  
Councilmember Lainez moved, seconded by Councilmember Garcia, to adopt a Resolution approving the Agreement with the County of Los Angeles for the Washington Blvd Traffic Signal Synchronization Program Project and allocating funds for the City's share of the project. The motion was carried by the following vote: 

AYES: Councilmembers Altamirano, Garcia, Lainez, Vice Mayor Argumedo and Mayor Rebollo. 

Item #6 - Acting Director of Public Works Nila provided an overview of the staff report. Councilmember Lainez asked who develops the plans for the improvements and how monies are spent. Director Nila responded that the group agrees to a cohesive plan before the Councils approve it. There is a formula that shows the proportional distribution. The grant is 100% reimbursable, and the City of Commerce up fronts the monies from Measure AA which will later be reimbursed. 

Discussion took place about bike lanes, design, and whether they are on the street. Acting Director Nila stated that during the planning phase, staff would consider safety, especially for those intersections at Eastern and Atlantic, to separate bike lanes from the vehicles. 

Vice Mayor Argumedo moved, seconded by Councilmember Lainez, to adopt a Resolution approving the Memorandum of Understanding with the City of Bell, the City of Huntington Park, and Los Angeles County for the Randolph Corridor Active Transportation Project. The motion was carried by the following vote: 

AYES: Councilmembers Altamirano, Garcia, Lainez, Vice Mayor Argumedo and Mayor Rebollo. 

Item #8 - Mayor Rebollo requested to continue this item for the next meeting. Mayor Rebollo moved, seconded by Councilmember Garcia, to continue this item to the next meeting. The motion was carried by the following vote: 

AYES: Councilmembers Altamirano, Garcia, Lainez, Vice Mayor Argumedo and Mayor Rebollo. 


4.. Agreement with Los Angeles County for the Olympic Boulevard Traffic Signal Synchronization Program

6.. Memorandum of Understanding with the City of Bell, City of Huntington Park, and Los Angeles County for the Randolph Corridor Active Transportation Project

5.. Agreement with Los Angeles County for the Washington Boulevard Traffic Signal Synchronization Program

7.. Revised Final Parcel Map No. 82490 for the Property Located at 6233 Telegraph Road and Located at the Northwest Corner of Washington and Telegraph Road

8.. Joint Powers Agreement Relating to the Membership in the Gateway Cities Affordable Housing Trust

3.. Approval of Minutes

2.. Approval of Warrant Register Nos. 11A, 11B, 11C, 12A, 12B, and 12C

SCHEDULED MATTERS

9.. Council Meeting Schedule - Rescheduling  February 14, 2023, to February 16, 2023

11.. Award of Construction Contract to J&S Striping Company, Inc. for the Mixmaster Striping and Pavement Marking Improvements Project  -  Action: adopt (Pass) Moved by Kevin Lainez Acting Director of Public Works Nila provided an overview of the staff report and a visual of the road markings. 

Discussion took place on whether there would be any street closures while improvements were made, to which Director Nila stated that it would be done at night time. Councilmember Garcia asked about the size of the road markings, and Director Nila indicated that it would be eight feet. 

Councilmember Lainez suggested that road markings are placed way in advance to allow motorists to adjust. 


12.. Committee and Commission Appointments Councilmember Lainez appointed Francheska Coreas to the Youth Advisory Commission.

ORDINANCES

13.. Introduction of Ordinance for First Reading Amending Commence Municipal Code, Title 9 “Peace, Safety and Morals” by Adding Chapter 9.82 “Unlawful Possession of Catalytic Converters”  -  Action: approve (Pass) Moved by Oralia Rebollo City Attorney Tapia provided an overview of the staff report. City Manager Cisneros stated that the City would utilize the media efforts to make residents aware of the Ordinance. Council Member Garcia asked whether there would be signage for the Ordinance, and the City Manager responded that there would be no signs installed. 

CITY COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY REPORTS Councilmember Lainez reported that he attended the Dia de Los Reyes event in January  and asked for an update on Parks and Recreation sports, hiring and how many applicants were Commerce residents, and how many were hired. 

ADJOURNMENT Meeting adjourned at 9:02 p.m. in memory of Jose Luis Gutierrez and Alfred Jaramillo, City of Commerce employee.
